seo_description: Free, open-source clipboard manager for macOS. A shelf of clipboard cards slides up with ⇧⌘C, with pinboards, keyboard paste, and no network access.
hero_sub: A strip of clipboard cards slides up from the bottom of your screen. Press ⇧⌘C, pick a card with the arrow keys, and hit Return to paste it into the app you were using.
features_sub: A native, keyboard-first clipboard history that stays on your Mac.

features.title: Clipboard history as cards
features.desc: Captures text, links, images and file references. Each card shows a type-aware preview, the source app's icon and a relative timestamp.

features.title: Keyboard-first control
features.desc: Use the arrow keys to browse, Return to paste, Space for a Quick Look popover, and just start typing to filter. The global hotkey is rebindable in Settings.

features.title: Pinboards for saved clips
features.desc: Create named pinboards as tabs, drag cards onto them, or press ⌘1 to ⌘9 to pin the selected card. Deleting a pinboard moves its cards back to History.

features.title: Opens on your current screen
features.desc: The translucent shelf appears at the bottom of the display your mouse is on. It switches to a solid background when Reduce Transparency is enabled.

features.title: Private and local only
features.desc: Skips items marked concealed or transient and ignores apps like Keychain Access and 1Password by default. You can also pause capture from the menu bar. No network requests are made.

features.title: Settings that fit your setup
features.desc: Choose a history length of 100, 500 or 1000, set the shelf height and card width, turn off image capture, and enable Launch at login.

permissions_step: Optionally grant Accessibility access in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility so ClipRibbonShelf can paste directly with ⌘V; without it, cards are copied and you press ⌘V yourself.

faq.q: Is ClipRibbonShelf really free and open source?
faq.a: Yes. It is released under the MIT license, with no account, subscription or paid tier. If it is useful to you, there is an optional Support button that links to Ko-fi.

Only Accessibility, and only so it can send ⌘V to the app you were using. You can decline it and still use everything else, since cards are copied and you press ⌘V yourself. It does not ask for Screen Recording, Microphone, Camera or network access.

faq.q: Where is my clipboard data stored?
faq.a: Only on your Mac, in ~/Library/Application Support/ClipRibbonShelf. History and pinboards are saved as JSON, with image files alongside. Nothing is sent anywhere.
Notarization requires a paid Apple Developer account, and this is a free project. Right-click the app and choose Open once to get past Gatekeeper, or build it yourself from source with Xcode.
